definition: Sounding harsh because the notes or voices fail to harmonise.
book: Around the World in Eighty Days
author: Jules Verne
quote: The discordant tones of the voices and instruments drew nearer, and now droning songs mingled with the sound of the tambourines and cymbals.
example_sentence: The orchestra tuning up made a discordant racket.
